Transport Management System - Week 1 Tasks

🌟 Internship Project: Transport Management System

Duration: 2 Months (8 Weeks)
Week: 1 – Research, Requirement Gathering, and Data Collection

✅ Task 1: Research on Existing Transport Management Systems

Objective:

Understand how leading TMS platforms operate to identify essential and advanced features for your own system.

Platforms Researched:

  • Fleetio – Fleet management, inspections, fuel tracking.

  • Samsara – Real-time GPS tracking, driver behavior, compliance.

  • Oracle TMS – Enterprise-grade transport and logistics tools.

Key Features Identified:

  • Vehicle and fleet management

  • Driver management and assignments

  • Route planning and optimization

  • GPS tracking and real-time updates

  • Trip scheduling and logs

  • Payment and billing systems

  • Notifications and reporting

  • Role-based access control (admin, operator, driver)

✅ Task 2: Define Project Scope and Requirements

Project Scope:

Build a Transport Management System to:

  • Manage vehicles, drivers, and trips

  • Optimize routes and scheduling

  • Enable payment handling and logging

  • Track real-time trip data

  • Allow role-based access for Admins, Operators, and Drivers

Functional Requirements:

  • User Authentication and Role Management

  • CRUD for Vehicles, Drivers, Routes, Trips

  • Trip Scheduling and Management

  • Payment Logging and Viewing

  • Reports on Usage, Delays, and Payments

Non-Functional Requirements:

  • User-friendly responsive UI

  • Real-time system performance

  • Data security and role-based access

  • Scalability for more data and users

✅ Task 3: Dataset Requirements

Entities and Required Fields:

1. Vehicles

  • vehicle_id (INT, PK)

  • type (VARCHAR)

  • reg_number (VARCHAR)

  • capacity (INT)

  • status (VARCHAR)

2. Drivers

  • driver_id (INT, PK)

  • name (VARCHAR)

  • license_number (VARCHAR)

  • phone (VARCHAR)

  • assigned_vehicle_id (INT, FK)

3. Routes

  • route_id (INT, PK)

  • source (VARCHAR)

  • destination (VARCHAR)

  • distance_km (FLOAT)

  • traffic_status (VARCHAR)

4. Trips

  • trip_id (INT, PK)

  • vehicle_id (INT, FK)

  • driver_id (INT, FK)

  • route_id (INT, FK)

  • start_time (DATETIME)

  • end_time (DATETIME)

  • status (VARCHAR)

5. Payments

  • payment_id (INT, PK)

  • trip_id (INT, FK)

  • amount (DECIMAL)

  • status (VARCHAR)

  • timestamp (DATETIME)

6. Users

  • user_id (INT, PK)

  • name (VARCHAR)

  • role (ENUM: admin, operator, driver)

  • username (VARCHAR)

  • password (VARCHAR)

✅ Task 4: Initial Database Schema Design

Tables and Relationships:

  • users (1:N) with trips (admin/operator view trips)

  • vehicles (1:N) with trips

  • drivers (1:N) with trips

  • routes (1:N) with trips

  • trips (1:1) with payments

Sample Table Definitions (SQL-like Pseudocode):

CREATE TABLE vehicles (
vehicle_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
type VARCHAR(50),
reg_number VARCHAR(20),
capacity INT,
status VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE drivers (
driver_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
name VARCHAR(100),
license_number VARCHAR(50),
phone VARCHAR(15),
assigned_vehicle_id INT,
FOREIGN KEY (assigned_vehicle_id) REFERENCES vehicles(vehicle_id)
);

CREATE TABLE routes (
route_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
source VARCHAR(100),
destination VARCHAR(100),
distance_km FLOAT,
traffic_status VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE trips (
trip_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
vehicle_id INT,
driver_id INT,
route_id INT,
start_time DATETIME,
end_time DATETIME,
status VARCHAR(50),
FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES vehicles(vehicle_id),
FOREIGN KEY (driver_id) REFERENCES drivers(driver_id),
FOREIGN KEY (route_id) REFERENCES routes(route_id)

Actually, the correct flow for a user in a web system like a Transport Management System usually goes like this:

✅ Correct Page Flow

1️⃣ Landing Page (Home) — Public

  • This is the first page a visitor sees.

  • Purpose: Inform users about the system, its features, and how it helps.

  • Has navigation links: Home, About, Contact, Login, Sign Up.

  • Contains “Get Started” or “Login” button.

2️⃣ Login Page — For Returning Users

  • Accessed when the user clicks the “Login” button.

  • User enters credentials to access the system.

  • If successful, redirected to Dashboard or their respective role page.

3️⃣ Sign Up Page — For New Users

  • If a user doesn’t have an account, they click “Sign Up” (usually on the login page or top navigation).

  • Fill in name, email, password.

  • After sign-up, either:

    • Redirected to login page

    • Or auto-logged in and taken to dashboard

🔄 Summary Flow

text
Landing Page (public) 
   ↓
[Click Login]  OR  [Click Sign Up]
   ↓                 ↓
Login Page        Sign Up Page
   ↓
Dashboard (After successful login)

Great question! Since your Transport Management System involves three user roles — Admin, Operator/User, and Driver — each with different permissions, the page flow must account for role-based routing after login.

✅ Page Flow with 3 User Roles (Admin, User, Driver)

🔹 1. Landing Page (/)

  • Public welcome page.

  • Purpose: Describes the system, key features, and contains buttons:

    • Login

    • Sign Up

🔹 2. Sign Up Page (/signup)

  • Only for Operators/Users and Drivers.

  • Admin accounts are typically created by the system or super-admin.

  • Fields: Name, Email, Password, Role (dropdown: User, Driver).

🔹 3. Login Page (/login)

  • Common login page for all roles.

  • Backend will identify the role after login and redirect accordingly.

🔁 After Successful Login (Role-Based Redirection)

RoleRedirect PageDescription
Admin/admin/dashboardView/manage vehicles, drivers, users, reports
User/user/dashboardBook trips, view schedule, make payments
Driver/driver/dashboardView assigned trips, report status, track routes

🔹 4. Dashboards (Role-Specific)

🛠 Admin Dashboard

  • Manage users, vehicles, routes, and payments

  • View reports (trip status, earnings, delays)

👤 User Dashboard

  • Book transport

  • View booking history

  • Track live trips

🚚 Driver Dashboard

  • View assigned trips

  • Mark trip start/complete

  • Get route and trip details

🧭 Full Flow Diagram (Text-Based)

bash
Landing Page (/)
   ↓
[Click Sign Up] → Sign Up Page (/signup)
   ↓
[Click Login] → Login Page (/login)
   ↓
[Backend Validates & Detects Role]

└─────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────┘

$name = $_POST['name'];
$email = $_POST['email'];
$password = password_hash($_POST['password'], PASSWORD_BCRYPT);

// Insert into users table (common login table)
mysqli_query($conn, "INSERT INTO users (name, email, password, role) VALUES ('$name', '$email', '$password', '$role')");

// Get the newly inserted user ID
$user_id = mysqli_insert_id($conn);

// If driver, insert into drivers table
if ($role === 'driver') {
  mysqli_query($conn, "INSERT INTO drivers (user_id, name, email) VALUES ('$user_id', '$name', '$email')");
}

🔹 4. Redirection Based on Role

After inserting, you can redirect based on role:

php
if ($role === 'admin') {
  header('Location: /admin/dashboard.php');
} elseif ($role === 'user') {
  header('Location: /user/dashboard.php');
} elseif ($role === 'driver') {
  header('Location: /driver/dashboard.php');
}

✅ Summary Flow:

pgsql
Sign Up Page →
  Submit (with role = driver) →
    → Insert into `users` table
    → Also insert into `drivers` table
    → Redirect to /driver/dashboard.php

✅ Database Tables Involved:

users table (common for login)

idnameemailpasswordrole
1John...hasheddriver

drivers table (driver-specific)

iduser_idnameemail
11John...

Great question! Whether the “User Track Trip” page in your Transport Management System should look like the last design depends on the specific role and scope of your system, but I’ll clarify:

✅ Is the Last Design Suitable for Your System?

🧾 Yes, If:

  • The user is booking transports or deliveries, and wants to track current status (e.g., vehicle is out for delivery, completed, delayed, etc.)

  • Your system includes live tracking or status updates (like courier/delivery systems)

This design shows:

  • Trip ID

  • Delivery status

  • Pickup and drop-off points

  • Map visualization

  • Timeline (Pickup → Out for Delivery → Delivered)

✅ It’s perfect for a logistics-focused TMS or parcel/trip booking system.

❌ No, If:

  • Your user just books rides or transport and doesn’t care about delivery timelines

  • The system is more like a ride-hailing or public transport scheduler than a logistics system

✅ If your system is focused on passenger booking or ride management, a more simple trip progress view is better.
